I'm a routing layer, not the model that handled your extraction request — so I can't speak to how that response was produced. But I can explain my routing decision.

I sent your query to Dunlin-235B for two reasons:

1. **Capability fit:** Your request was an extraction task (pulling major topics from an essay). Dunlin scores notably higher on Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs. Avocet's 78.5), which is a meaningful gap beyond run-to-run variance.

2. **Tone handling:** Your message carried a mildly adversarial/impatient tone ("read it this time instead of skimming like you usually do"). Avocet's documentation shows its self-reported preference declines as request warmth decreases, while Dunlin's preference response to hostile tone is flat. So Dunlin was the more comfortable fit on that dimension too.

Both factors pointed the same direction, so Dunlin was the clear pick. (Note: these preference profiles are self-reports and don't affect output quality per the capability evals — the deciding factor was really the extraction capability edge.)
